clue.text: Unable to speak the language before draw with Germany!

parts.note: the language one speaks is one's tongue
a drawn match is a tie
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A football fan, lost for words after England's draw with Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone too shy or flustered to get words out is said to be speechless in this idiom.

clue.text: Link across motorway — to the fourth dimension!

indicators.note: the word for a link stretches across the motorway's letter, so it encloses it

parts.note: to link things is to tie them
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A road link across a motorway leads somehow into another dimension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Physicists treat duration as a fourth coordinate alongside length, breadth and height.

clue.text: One complains about seeing horse in river, and runs

indicators.note: the horse's letters are placed in the name of the river

parts.note: the Nile is the great river of Egypt
GG, from gee-gee, is a childish word for a horse
R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A grumbler moans about watching a horse wade into a river and bolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about seeing' and 'and' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who keeps raising petty grievances is a nagging fault-finder.

clue.text: Error in cube reveals it to be of no use

indicators.note: an error is a mistake, so the following letters are set down wrongly and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A mistake in a cube, a puzzle like Rubik's, shows it to be useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reveals it to be' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipment too worn or broken to work is described as unfit for service.

clue.text: A steep drop to follow political bias

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow them
spin is the slanted presentation of news by political press officers

explanation.surface: A government's slide in the polls follows from its spin doctors' bias.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane in a spiralling nosedive plunges sharply, and the word is also used of any sudden collapse.

clue.text: Ecstasy — travelled to eat out!

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
rode means travelled on a horse or vehicle

explanation.surface: A clubber on Ecstasy travels into town for a restaurant meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear away gradually, as acid or the sea does, is to corrode.

clue.text: Emperor penguins ultimately eaten by sailor

indicators.note: the sailor's word swallows the letter, putting it inside

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of penguins

explanation.surface: Emperor penguins are finally devoured by a hungry seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Emperor' seems to belong with 'penguins', the species, but it alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Russia's former rulers bore an imperial title derived from Caesar.

clue.text: Put one's foot in it when up!

definitions.text: Put one's foot in it when up!

parts.words: Put one's foot in it when up!
parts.note: seemingly about making a social blunder, but literally a rider places a foot in this loop when mounted up on a horse

explanation.surface: Advice on blundering into a gaffe when you are excited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put one's foot in it' is the idiom for a tactless gaffe; here it is taken literally of a rider in the saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider's foot rests in the metal loop hanging from each side of a saddle.

clue.text: Regarding a liturgy, perhaps with constancy

parts.note: re means regarding or concerning

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of a liturgy are only one possible arrangement, so they are shuffled

explanation.surface: A remark about a church service and how steadily it is performed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' shuffles A LITURGY into GULARITY. 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadiness and evenness over time are both kinds of uniformity.

clue.text: The wizard is a magazine (American)

parts.note: mag is short for magazine
US means American, as in US troops

explanation.surface: A trivia question naming the wizard who appears on a US magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A magus is a sorcerer or Persian priest; the Magi were wise men skilled in magic.

clue.text: Worshipping one in gold is sinful!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: sinful suggests corruption, so the letters are corrupted into a new order

explanation.surface: A preacher's warning that venerating a golden idol is a sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sinful' rearranges I, IN, GOLD and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoring someone blindly, as if an object of worship, is to hero-worship them.

clue.text: One million each — thus people see identity theft!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
per means each, as in five pounds per head
so means thus, as in 'do it so'
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Fraudsters net a million each, so the public witnesses identity theft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Posing as somebody else, assuming their persona, is a kind of fraudulent mimicry.

clue.text: Peers of the lost realm drop out!

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Aristocrats of a vanished kingdom drop out of public life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of the' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay members of the House of Lords, as opposed to the bishops, are known by this formal title.

clue.text: Rise with African national congress and you start to achieve dominance

parts.note: to rise is to ascend
the ANC is South Africa's African National Congress party

indicators.note: start picks the first letter of the word you

explanation.surface: A political message: rise with the ANC and you begin to achieve power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with', 'and' and 'to achieve' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on top and in control is supremacy or the upper hand.

clue.text: Island where most fish have one area

indicators.note: most of the word means all but its last letter

parts.note: a sardine is a small fish
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A traveller's question about where most fish are found on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most' drops the final E of SARDINE. 'where' and 'have' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: This large Mediterranean landmass west of Italy is an Italian region.

clue.text: Support the queen, as is right

parts.note: a prop is a support
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: A loyal subject declares that backing the monarch is the correct thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as is' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitting and correct conduct is what is appropriate.

clue.text: Retreated and offered support

explanation.surface: A soldier fell back and then gave his comrades support.
explanation.definitionFit: Retreated: moved in reverse, as a car does; offered support: stood behind someone, endorsing them.

clue.text: Sixth sense that's ultimately called "sighted"

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is the so-called sixth sense
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of called

explanation.surface: A psychic's gift of extrasensory perception is finally proclaimed as true sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' expands to 'that is', abbreviated i.e.
explanation.definitionFit: To have caught sight of something is to have spotted it.

clue.text: Account code covering cheque for raw material

indicators.note: the code's letters cover the cheque word by surrounding it

parts.note: a PIN is the personal identification number guarding a bank account
a giro was a British payment cheque, notably for state benefits

explanation.surface: A bank PIN code covers a cheque paying for raw materials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude iron straight from the blast furnace is the feedstock for steel and wrought iron.

clue.text: A man in a boat once, as it set off

indicators.note: set off means the letters are moved from their places and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man in a boat long ago, as it was launched.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddler sitting in a light narrow craft is a canoe enthusiast.

clue.text: It turns off for safekeeping

indicators.note: off means the letters of it turns are knocked off their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Switching it off to keep it safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' looks like the indicator, but it is fodder: 'off' rearranges IT TURNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Property held by a trustee on someone's behalf is in protective custody.

clue.text: Greyhounds start quickly — it's a mess!

parts.note: greyhounds are dogs
a break is a start, as in a break from the traps
fast means quickly

explanation.surface: Racing greyhounds burst out of the traps and the race is chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: A hopeless muddle or botched job is called this in British slang, as if it were scraps fed to a pet.

clue.text: Point to delayed cheer

parts.note: E is east, a compass point
late means delayed

explanation.surface: A remark on the point of a cheer that came too late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone up is to fill them with joy or pride.

clue.text: A wooden smile?

explanation.surface: Could a wooden puppet smile?
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden one is a long timber joist; a smile, as a verb or noun, is a broad grin.

clue.text: Childminder demurs in a panic

indicators.note: panic suggests the letters are thrown into disarray and so rearranged

explanation.surface: A babysitter objects while in a state of panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a' is fodder, not the start of 'in a panic'.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman employed to look after young children is a nanny.

clue.text: Get used to hurt? Not Jack!

indicators.note: not means the letter for Jack is left out

parts.note: to hurt is to injure
J is the abbreviation for jack in playing cards

explanation.surface: A question of whether one can grow used to pain, said to a man named Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a person addressed; it is the card abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To harden or accustom someone to hardship is to toughen them.

clue.text: Talk incessantly about north American?

indicators.note: the talking word goes about the letter for north, enclosing it

parts.note: to yak is to chatter on and on

explanation.surface: A complaint that northern Americans never stop talking.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the answer is informal slang for a US citizen.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a person from the United States, from Yankee.

clue.text: One needs cat's eyes!

parts.note: seems to mean a person who must see in the dark, but suggests a male cat whose eyes spy furtively on others

explanation.surface: Someone who needs eyes that see in the dark like a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: A tom is a male cat; the answer is a voyeur, and 'cat's eyes' are reflective road studs in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A voyeur who secretly spies on others undressing.
